title: Game dev beginner and study hobbyist
author: DrikoEl
selftext:
Hi there. I’m starting to make a game as a learning project; I’m studying Digital Game Programming and chose Godot because its scripting language is very similar to Python.

I’m facing a major challenge, though. I want to create an RPG/farming-sim style game because it allows me to apply everything I’ve learned so far while also picking up new skills. The issue lies with tilesets and characters/NPCs. Since this is a study project, I have a zero-dollar budget, but I still want the game to look good. Could you recommend any free AI tools for generating tilesets, characters/NPCs, and other assets? The free resources I’ve found online so far are quite limited.

Thanks in advance to everyone.

comments.author: EDWARDPIPER93
comments.body:
look at [opengameart.org](http://opengameart.org) 

there is so much stuff there it's not worth generating new stuff if you're starting out and just need filler

comments.author: ParticularGur2193
comments.body: It's not the answer you want but I really think that if you want to make games especially RPG games I highly recommend learning pixel art, it's easy and it's so much more rewarding to have something that you have made yourself instead of just prompting something to an AI, I'm studying game dev rn and making a fantasy rpg with pixel art and i can tell u that theres a lot of people who isn't gonna want to play it if it's ai generated, there's a lot of free pixel art sites like resprite. Pixel art can also be so detailed and look so good even In 2d or 3d.

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: It’s so sad to hear comments like this if someone uses ai, id be curious to hear WHY would there be so many people that won’t play it because it uses ai art?

replies.author: ParticularGur2193
replies.body:
I think mainly because the lack of quality in ai games, aswell as the lack of personality and time and effort put into the games. The gaming industry is at its core creativity and AI is an insult to the human creativity.
Would u rather have good from a Michelin star restaurant where people have worked and studied for years to perfect their craft or would u like a pizza from a vending machine. 
If you don't want to put in the work then just say that you are lazy. 
Art isn't talent it's work same with game development .

replies.author: Square_Reason_6490
replies.body: Sure I would love Michelin Star food but I also love a good hole in the wall or some fast food joint where people may not have studied for years, also I would eat a microwave pizza whose buttons were pressed by a Michelin star chef,art is not how long it took to make it, there are many amazing artists that make amazing work in seconds. If we apply your logic to communicating some would say you are lazy for typing and talking with people on the internet. Art is much bigger than talk or work it’s a means to communicate. I just hate to see people be so negative towards others who choose to try something different

replies.author: Ok_Pea_8752
replies.body:
alot of people basicly dont think for themselves. they just hop onto others opinion and then voice that and when they hear what they say they get emberresed like this guy and removes every trace of it. 

i remember reading a study where people was to judge Paintings from AI and from real Artists. Basicly every1 in the study choose the one they were told was the artists work, but in reality both pieces was the work of the artist, almost every1 voted for the one they believed and was told was the artists work. comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Free assets packs would probably be better time spent especially if you have it done anything art wise with gen AI you will subpar results if not fluent in prompting and digital art design

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
What is your AI of choice? Just try generating some images and try to make them consistent. It is for learning, right? Just dive into it

Dedicated tools are more convenient but they are usually not free

comments.author: Square_Reason_6490
comments.body: My advice would be to use the free game assets to start much faster can be super ugly, once you get a base for the game stood up and working you can decide how to go about the art, you could always also take that free game art and repurpose/remix that with ai to get a new look it can be a pain in the ass to get ai art get rdy, sizes off change design. For art ai I would suggest midjourney and you edit the images by hand Photoshop or whatever you use for image editing, use ChatGPT or nano banana to edit as well, I would experiment with those tools to build stuff like timesheets as well and to make multiple assets consistent. At this stage I think the key is to move fast and break stuff and let your game reveal itself to you
